evals.prompt: I'm building an evaluator for a visual node-based image-authoring graph. Some nodes (blur, compress, bake) are expensive, and the same subtree gets evaluated repeatedly across edits. Design the caching scheme that decides when a node can reuse a previously computed output instead of recomputing it. Explain exactly what the cache key is computed from and the one mistake that would make it return stale results.
assertions: States the cache key (validity hash) is computed from the node's own settings combined with the validity hashes of all of its inputs
Warns that omitting any consumed input from the hash produces silent stale reuse with no error, so every input that affects the output must be folded in

evals.prompt: In my node-graph tool, authors can select a group of nodes and collapse them into a single reusable subgraph node that can be dropped into other graphs. How should the runtime evaluator handle these subgraph nodes, and what must I guard against so a user can't crash the tool by nesting subgraphs?
assertions: Says subgraphs are flattened/inlined into the parent at compile time so the evaluator sees one flat DAG and never recurses into subgraphs at runtime
Warns that a subgraph transitively containing itself would inline forever / overflow the stack, so cycles must be detected and rejected before inlining

evals.prompt: I'm implementing the wiring logic for a node editor. A node has typed input and output pins. Walk me through the rules for what makes a connection legal, how many wires each pin may accept, when type checking happens, and what to do when a user tries to wire a CPU-memory image output into a node that expects a GPU image.
assertions: States each input pin accepts at most one source wire while an output pin may fan out to many consumers
Says connection type validity is checked at author/connect time (not deferred to evaluation)
Requires an explicit conversion node (e.g. upload/readback) for CPU-vs-GPU image mismatch rather than silently coercing

evals.prompt: Design the in-memory and on-disk representation for a procedural content node graph so the editor, evaluator, and diff/merge tools all read the same thing, and plugins can add new node kinds. How should the graph be stored, and how do terminal nodes that produce a rendered image or a draw call actually get that work executed?
assertions: Represents the graph as plain serialized data (explicit node list plus connection list plus per-node settings), not topology buried in imperative code
States that terminal/output nodes only surface a result and the owning system schedules the emitted work; if no system consumes the output node the work never runs
